hourly.summary: The football discussion centers on familiar Arsenal anxieties: the men's team leaking long-range goals and getting 'bullied' in midfield by Brighton, while Liverpool fend off interest in youngster Rio Ngumoha. Bright spots exist — Max Dowman's England call-up, the Women's team gearing up for UCL duty against HB Køge, and praise for Adrian Clarke's punditry — but the overall mood is that of a fanbase gnawing on defensive frailties and transfer near-misses. The forum itself appears distracted by a passionate, multi-post debate about £4 mangoes.

daily.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment deteriorated sharply throughout the day following the 3-0 loss at Brighton, shifting from a sober, perspective-tinged disappointment in the early hours to a full-blown crisis by evening. Morning analysis focused on tactical questions and fixture congestion context, but afternoon brought Arteta's stinging 'lack of respect' critique, xG-fueled finishing fury, and rival schadenfreude. By nightfall, the mood had collapsed into outright despair — defence exposed, title talk dead, and even the women's draw compounding a 'thoroughly miserable weekend'.

weekly.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment traced a dramatic boom-and-bust arc across the week: cautious optimism early on built into bullish, title-chasing euphoria by mid-week, only to implode catastrophically after a 3-0 loss at Brighton on the 19th. The final two days saw sentiment plummet from peak confidence (8/10) to meltdown and despair (3/10), with Arteta's 'lack of respect' critique, exposed defensive frailties, and extinguished title hopes defining a thoroughly miserable finish.
